title: We Bless the Prophet of the Lord
description: We Bless the Prophet of the Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 132, headed “The offices of Christ”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We bless the Pro-phet of the Lord, That comes with truth and grace; Je-sus, thy Spir-it and thy word Shall lead us in thy ways.

lines: We bless the Prophet of the Lord,
That comes with truth and grace;
Jesus, thy Spirit and thy word
Shall lead us in thy ways.
We reverence our High Priest above,
And lives to carry on his love,
He guards our souls from hell and sin
His mercies lay a sovereign claim

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
